newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica black home expenditure seen soaring - study.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica black home expenditure seen soaring - study.

text.p: Household expenditure in black areas in South Africa is expected to soar by the year 2010, a survey released on Wednesday showed.

BMI Building Research Strategy consultants said high income households -- black and white -- currently spent around 11.38 billion rand annually on home improvements, of which about 700 million rand was spent by black households.
"But this figure is expected to soar to eight billion by 2010, equalling the amount spent by Super A-income white households," the survey said.
The research found that almost half of the black households surveyed had built-on, added or improved their homes in the last five years in line with an increase in home ownership and higher incomes.

The most frequent type of home improvement was the addition of a bedroom, followed by a bathroom. Other popular improvements included the installation of wall-to-wall carpeting, ceilings and painting.
Over 60 percent of black household respondents said they would like to improve their homes further in the next 12 months.
The installation of ceramic floor tiles topped the "to do" list of most families followed by installation of kitchen cupboards, burglar bars and a new front door.
